steps.text: In a medium bowl, combine the mayonnaise, pepper, salt, lemon juice, vinegar and sugar. Mix all together until smooth. Use to baste chicken, pork chops or ribs as they cook on the grill. Serve extra as dipping sauce!

raw_recipe.headline: White BBQ Sauce
raw_recipe.description: Mayonnaise and lemon juice with vinegar make a creamy, tart sauce that is a nice break from tomato barbecue sauces. Also serves well as a dipping sauce. This one is a keeper, too--lasts for weeks in the fridge.
raw_recipe.name: White BBQ Sauce

recipeInstructions.text: In a medium bowl, combine the mayonnaise, pepper, salt, lemon juice, vinegar and sugar. Mix all together until smooth. Use to baste chicken, pork chops or ribs as they cook on the grill. Serve extra as dipping sauce!

review.reviewBody: This "white sauce" was made famous at Big Bob Gibson's BBQ in North Alabama. Several things are left out in this recipe such as horseradish and apple cider vinegar. Let it sit for a few hours to overnight and it really melds the taste.

This sauce is incredible.. the trick is to make it up..put it in the fridge and dont touch it for at least 24 to 36 hours..it takes that long for the flavors to mingle..if you taste it too early it is awful and too sweet. I did make it with 4 packages of splenda instead of sugar..I found that I like making a bowl of salad, adding a pile of bbq brisket on top, and using this as the salad dressing also

I used this recipe to make White BBQ chicken salad for a ladies luncheon and it was a big hit with everyone going back for seconds. I halved the recipe then I cooked 5 chicken breasts in my crock pot in chicken broth until they were so tender they shredded easily with a fork. I added the (halved) sauce and a few ribs of celery cut up then baked it at 300 for about 20 minutes the night before the luncheon. The next day I pulled it out of the fridge an served it with Hawaiian sweet rolls. P.S. I used real mayo not Miracle Whip as some have suggested.

i haven't made this recipe yet Ive been looking for white bbq sauces since i saw it on the food network they say white bbq sauce is best for bird meat and burgers and a different recipe i saw for it that got 5 stars included the exact same everything but also had a tbs of hoarse radish and a clove of garlic and a tsp of ground clove i will be making this minus all the salt :)

Way way way too much salt. Two tablespoons for two cups of Mayo is about 5 times the amount of salt you would need. I would suggest starting with 1/2 teaspoon and adjust from there. I had to throw out the first batch I made due to the excessive salt. Otherwise a good starter recipe. Bobs from AL also includes horseradish and a I like touch of cayenne. Beware of the salt.
I made a slight variation of this recipe, substituted lime juice for lemon juice (only 3 tablespoons). It was fantastic and definitely something I will make again! Thanks for sharing this recipe.

This sauce was delicious! It was slightly thick because of the mayonnaise so it adhered well to the meat. I added a couple chopped green onions and some hot sauce to the marinade for a bit of a kick and it worked out great. Then I cooked the leftover sauce and drizzled it over the meat once it was done. Yummy!!

I am from Decatur, AL where we love our White Sauce! For those of you that this is too salty for only add 1 tblsp at a time and taste. However I would cut the lemon juice to only 2 tblsp. and never use Miracle Whip! Great to smoke chicken, turkey or pork. Also a great dipping sauce.

I just seen it made on tv @ big bobs bbq it was apple juice. along with some red pepper which looked to be cayenne pepper,horseradish,white vinegar,lemmon juice,black pepper,salt,sugar and of course mayo
Good stuff! I replace the white vinegar with equal amount of Chiavetta's marinade (Upstate NY staple) and it is pure awesome.

This bbq sauce is my secret to great grilled chicken! I always make extra sauce so I can marinade the chicken as well. I put both the sauce and the marinating chicken in the fridge overnight to meld all the flavors. Then I just throw the chicken on the grill, baste a little as I go, and serve the sauce on the side. Yum! My husband also likes to dip his chicken nuggets in this sauce!
Made it twice now and definitely will make again! Super easy and tastes great! Great for family with night shade allergies that can't eat regular BBQ sauce.
With a bit less salt, this recipe would be perfect!
My mom asks for this every time i smoke chickens
This sauce came out gross. I added several other seasonings and a splash of steak sauce to it and rescued it as a tangy dip. I'd be offended if someone served this on my bbq....
This has topped my list of BBQ sauces. LOVE this sauce and use it as my main sauce on grilled chicken. Delicious!
I've never had the original in Alabama. All I can say is, as a lover of BBQ sauce, this is really unique and good. It's a new staple in my BBQ sauce rotation.
I made this exactly as written, but my brother in law was the only person brave enough to taste it. He said it was "ok" and nobody else would go near it.
This came out very thin although it sat for over a day. My husband added horseradish, but overall, we did not care for it. We love it in a local restaurant, but this really did not compare.

My husband is from Alabama and said he missed this this little bit of home, so i came to find a recipe for it- - He loves it, so far we have used it on pork chops, chicken, and ribs. Its great on everything!
